historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-12.5% 3yr, -3.2% 5yr) diverges far more than 30% from revenue; book value has been destroyed by Monsanto impairments (FY2020, FY2023-24) and litigation charges, not by the operating trend, so it is not a usable growth anchor. EPS CAGRs undefined (FY2023-25 statutory losses). Revenue 5yr CAGR (FY2020 base, not distorted at the sales line) selected.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (SBC zero, no interest-income strip), so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs coincide. Reported FCF is after litigation payouts and therefore noisy (FY2021 2,478 to FY2025 3,443).

scenario_narratives.base: Bayer stabilises rather than re-rates. FY2026 lands inside guidance (sales EUR44.7-47.0bn, EBITDA bsi ~EUR9.8bn) and the ~EUR5bn of Roundup/PCB payouts extinguish provisions already deducted in the bridge. Pharma's five growth catalysts roughly offset the Xarelto generic and Eylea biosimilar cliffs through FY2028 and then add ~2-3% a year; Crop Science grows low single digits on Preceon corn and new chemistry against generic glyphosate pricing. The Dynamic Shared Ownership cost base lifts EBITDA bsi to ~22.5% by FY2030, of which ~0.5pp leaks to restructuring and unprovisioned new claims. Unlevered FCF ~EUR5bn rising to ~EUR7bn; terminal capped at 13x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Durnell 7-2 FIFRA preemption ruling and final approval of the US$7.25bn class settlement end the Roundup tail, the provision proves adequate and the BBB negative outlook turns stable, freeing capital for growth. Asundexian (OCEANIC-STROKE positive) is approved and becomes a blockbuster alongside Nubeqa, Kerendia and Beyonttra; Crop's 10-launches-in-10-years framework delivers; EBITDA bsi reaches management's mid-20s target (24.5% after leakage) by FY2031. Mid-single-digit growth through FY2030; terminal 15x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Litigation is contained but not closed: opt-outs from the class settlement, new PCB claims (NC State Poe Hall) and the EPA glyphosate re-evaluation keep ~EUR0.7bn/yr of cash flowing outside the provision. Xarelto and Eylea decline faster than launches ramp, Consumer Health keeps lagging Haleon/Kenvue, and generic glyphosate plus the dicamba vacatur pin Crop margins. EBITDA after leakage stalls at ~18.5%, growth ~1.5%, and the leverage leaves no room for a re-rating; terminal 11x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the operating businesses on unlevered owner FCF before litigation, and charge the litigation exactly once as a balance-sheet claim (provisions + agreed settlements, net of the tax shield). The equity is a thin slice between a ~EUR85bn enterprise and ~EUR44bn of debt-like claims, so small changes in margin or exit multiple move per-share value a lot; the bear/bull spread is the honest measure of that leverage.
key_risks_to_valuation: Litigation reserves prove inadequate (opt-outs, PCB, EPA glyphosate review) - every EUR1bn of extra claims is ~EUR0.80/share after tax
Pharma patent cliff (Xarelto, Eylea) outruns the launch portfolio
Crop Science margin pressure from generic glyphosate and regulatory deregistrations
Rating downgrade below BBB raising refinancing cost on EUR33bn of bonds
Balance-sheet anchor is FY2025; H1-2026 interim not extracted

inputs.share_count_basis: 982.42m shares, FY2025 annual report; no dilutive securities (LTI plans are cash-settled). Held flat: no buyback, no SBC, no equity raise planned (the Apollo LARC deal was a subsidiary minority stake, not Bayer AG equity).
inputs.sbc_source: No equity-settled share-based payment: Bayer's LTI (Aspire / Bayer Performance Shares) is cash-settled and already charged in personnel expense and EBITDA. SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:21Z (Xetra regular session, last close before valuation date)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR build. Rf 2.7% (10y Bund), ERP 5.5%, levered beta 1.3 (BBB/Baa2 negative-outlook balance sheet, debt-like claims ~EUR44bn vs ~EUR43bn market cap) -> CoE ~9.9%. After-tax cost of debt ~2.8% (BBB EUR ~3.8% pre-tax, 27% shield). Weights ~59% equity / 41% net financial debt -> WACC ~7.0%. Same 7.0% in every scenario: litigation and pipeline risk are charged in the bridge and the bear flows, not stacked as a discount-rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: the EUR1,286m lease liabilities sit inside Bayer's net financial debt (29,843), EBITDA is post-IFRS-16 with no lease charge, and ~0.4pp of revenue is added to capex for right-of-use renewals.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI deducted once in the bridge: legacy NCI EUR116m plus the EUR3.0bn Apollo stake in the LARC entity (July 2026), offset by the EUR3.0bn cash received, which is not yet in the Dec-2025 net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating conglomerate: Crop Science ~47%, Pharma ~39%, Consumer Health ~13%), with the non-US adaptations (EUR WACC, SBC-zero, lease treatment A, NCI in bridge). Litigation handled as a balance-sheet claim, not a flow: the FY2025 litigation provisions (EUR10,811m, AR note 23) plus the EUR978m reclassified to other liabilities for agreed settlements = EUR11,789m deducted in the equity bridge, with a ~20% US tax shield credited separately. The flows therefore start from EBITDA before special items, less a haircut for recurring non-litigation special items (DSO restructuring, EUR0.5-1.2bn/yr in FY24-25) and a small allowance for unprovisioned new claims (PCB). This is why the guided negative FY2026 FCF (EUR-1.5 to -2.5bn incl. ~EUR5bn settlement payouts) does NOT appear in the flows: those payouts extinguish the provision deducted in the bridge, so including them in the flows would charge them twice. FY0 base is FY2025 (EBITDA bsi 9,669, 21.2%; EBIT bsi 5,108, D&A bsi 4,561 = 10.0% of sales; capex 2,487; cash tax 1,243). FY2020 (EBIT ~-16bn impairments) is not used as a base for anything. last_fcf = reported FCF (OCF 5,930 - capex 2,487) because SBC is zero and Bayer is net-debt so interest income is not stripped; note that reported FCF is after ~EUR1.7bn of litigation cash outflows in FY2025. STALENESS: balance sheet is FY2025 (31 Dec 2025); the H1-2026 interim (Aug 2026) is not extracted. The bridge is roughly invariant to that: H1 settlement payouts move a provision into net debt one-for-one, and the Apollo proceeds are bridged explicitly. Replace with the Q3-2026 balance sheet when extracted. Buybacks: none (value-neutral here because no SBC). Dividend held at the EUR0.11 legal minimum.

bear.narrative: Settlement opt-outs, new PCB suits and the EPA glyphosate review keep ~EUR0.7bn/yr of unprovisioned litigation cash flowing; Xarelto/Eylea erosion outruns launches; generic glyphosate and dicamba vacatur keep Crop margins depressed.

base.narrative: FY2026 at guidance (EBITDA bsi EUR9.6-10.1bn, ~-2pp FX), then Nubeqa/Kerendia/Beyonttra/Lynkuet backfill Xarelto and Eylea erosion and Crop grows low single digits; EBITDA bsi creeps to ~22.5% as DSO savings land, less ~0.5pp ongoing unprovisioned litigation.

bull.narrative: Durnell preemption plus class settlement approval close the Roundup tail; asundexian approved, Preceon and the Crop 10-blockbuster framework land; management reaches its mid-20s EBITDA bsi margin target.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: ~EUR44bn of debt-like claims against a ~EUR43bn market cap, BBB/Baa2 negative outlook, and the class settlement still awaiting final approval with opt-out termination rights. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs litigation closure AND asundexian AND the margin target, three largely independent outcomes, even after the Supreme Court win removed the worst tail. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.
